reviews.rationale: This is a circRNA/miRNA-focused review that only lists LSS, FDPS, and PMVK (as PMK) as known KEGG pathway members in background/introductory text; it presents no original gene-specific data or experimental system for any of these genes. Declared 'indirect' context implies a specific comparator biological system, but the source is a pure biochemistry synthesis with no experimental context at all.

evidence_span.text: we generated ERG28 KO human liver cell lines and showed they have reduced production and, under sterol-depleted conditions, when cells depend on de novo cholesterol synthesis, reduced overall levels of cholesterol.

reviews.rationale: CRISPR KO of ERG28 in the human liver cell line Huh7 causally reduces de novo cholesterol synthesis and impairs SREBP-2 processing, directly supporting Erg28's assigned non-catalytic scaffold role in hepatocyte cholesterol biosynthesis; NanoBiT interaction assays also generated gene-specific data for Nsdhl and Msmo1 (as SC4MOL) but only as ERG28-binding partners, not as tests of their own catalytic function. Human hepatoma cell line context reasonably matches the declared 'partial' context relative to mouse primary hepatocytes.

The abstract cites MVK mutation/Mevalonate kinase deficiency only as disease-context motivation; the actual experiment uses Lovastatin to block the pathway and tests 25-hydroxycholesterol in a human glioblastoma line, with no MVK-specific perturbation or gene-specific data generated. MVK is background-only here, so it cannot be credited as studied or function-supported for the hepatocyte mevalonate-pathway mechanism.
